description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify relationships between corresponding terms and form ordered pairs.
Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as in the place to its right and 1/10 of the place to its left.
Explain patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.
Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
Find whole-number quotients with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using place-value strategies.
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using place-value strategies and written methods.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by rewriting with like denominators.
Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators.
Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator; solve related word problems.
Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction; find areas of rectangles with fractional side lengths.
Interpret multiplication as scaling by comparing product size based on the factors without always computing.
Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions; solve related real-world problems.
Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a system and use conversions in multi-step problems.
Make a line plot of fractional measurements and use fraction operations to solve problems from the data.
Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement with unit cubes.
Measure volumes by counting unit cubes using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.
Relate volume to multiplication and addition; find volumes of rectangular prisms and additive solid figures.
Use perpendicular number lines (axes) to define a coordinate system and locate points by ordered pairs.
Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant and interpret coordinates.
Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories.
Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.
Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language.
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, including percents and unit conversions.
Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.
Find GCF of two whole numbers ≤ 100 and LCM of two whole numbers ≤ 12; use the distributive property with common factors.
Understand that positive and negative numbers describe opposite directions or values; represent quantities in real-world contexts.
Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend axes to represent points with negative coordinates.
Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers; interpret inequalities and magnitude in context.
Solve problems by graphing points in all four quadrants; use coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points.
Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
Identify when two expressions are equivalent (they name the same number for any substitution).
Understand solving an equation or inequality as finding which values from a set make it true; use substitution.
Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving real-world or mathematical problems.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q.
Write inequalities of the form x > c or x < c and represent solutions on number line diagrams.
Use variables for related quantities; write an equation for the dependent variable and analyze with graphs and tables.
Find areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing or decomposing shapes.
Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths using unit cubes and volume formulas.
Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given vertices; use coordinates to find side lengths.
Represent three-dimensional figures using nets of rectangles and triangles, and use nets to find surface area.
Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question.
Understand that a data set has a distribution that can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.
Recognize that a measure of center summarizes values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes spread.
Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.
Summarize numerical data sets in context, including measures of center (median/mean) and variability.
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including lengths, areas, and other quantities.
Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities, including the constant of proportionality.
Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers.
Multiply and divide rational numbers; convert a rational number to a terminating or repeating decimal.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms can shed light on the problem and related quantities.
Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems with positive and negative rational numbers in any form.
Use variables to construct simple equations and inequalities to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas.
Draw geometric shapes with given conditions; focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides.
Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures.
Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.
Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles to solve for an unknown angle.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of 2D and 3D objects.
Understand that statistics about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative.
Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population; gauge variation in estimates.
Informally assess visual overlap of two distributions; express difference of centers as a multiple of variability.
Use measures of center and variability from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences.
Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 expressing likelihood.
Approximate probability by long-run relative frequency; predict approximate relative frequency given a probability.
Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events; compare to observed frequencies.
Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.
Know that irrational numbers are not rational; show repeating decimals and convert repeating decimals to rationals.
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare sizes, locate on a number line, and estimate expressions.
Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
Use square root and cube root symbols; evaluate roots of small perfect squares and cubes; know √2 is irrational.
Use single-digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities and compare them.
Perform operations with numbers in scientific notation, including mixed decimal and scientific notation problems.
Graph proportional relationships, interpreting unit rate as slope; compare proportional relationships in different forms.
Use similar triangles to explain constant slope; derive y = mx and y = mx + b.
Solve linear equations in one variable, including cases with one, infinitely many, or no solutions.
Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations algebraically and by graphing.
Understand that a function assigns to each input exactly one output; the graph is the set of input-output ordered pairs.
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically, or verbally).
Interpret y = mx + b as a linear function; give examples of functions that are not linear.
Construct a function to model a linear relationship; determine rate of change and initial value from a description or values.
Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph; sketch qualitative graphs.
Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations on lines, angles, and parallel lines.
Understand congruence via sequences of rotations, reflections, and translations; describe a congruence sequence.
Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.
Understand similarity via rigid motions and dilations; describe a sequence that exhibits similarity.
Use informal arguments about triangle angle sum, exterior angles, transversal angles, and AA similarity.
Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in 2D and 3D problems.
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.
Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world problems.
Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data; describe patterns of association.
For scatter plots suggesting linear association, informally fit a straight line and assess model fit.
Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in bivariate measurement data, interpreting slope and intercept.
Construct and interpret two-way tables of bivariate categorical data; use relative frequencies to describe association.
